title: Why Team Effectiveness Is a Business Advantage
summary: By the Automation Enabling Technologies Team Organizations often focus on improving strategy, processes, and technology to drive performance. Yet one of the most powerful performance drivers is often overlooked: how effectively teams work together. As businesses grow, leaders are increasingly asked to solve complex problems across functions, disciplines, and regions. Success depends not only on expertise, but on […]
body_text: By the Automation Enabling Technologies Team Organizations often focus on improving strategy, processes, and technology to drive performance. Yet one of the most powerful performance drivers is often overlooked: how effectively teams work together. As businesses grow, leaders are increasingly asked to solve complex problems across functions, disciplines, and regions. Success depends not only on expertise, but on the ability to collaborate effectively with people who may think, communicate, and make decisions differently. Recently, leaders within our Automation Enabling Technologies business participated in a team development experience designed to strengthen collaboration by helping individuals better understand one another’s working styles and decision-making approaches. The experience reinforced an important reality: differences within a team are not obstacles to overcome. They are assets that can improve decision-making when understood and leveraged effectively. Teams perform better when members understand what motivates one another, how they process information, how they respond to stress, and where they naturally contribute their strongest value. That awareness reduces friction, builds trust, and creates more productive conversations. It also helps teams identify blind spots. Every team develops patterns over time. Some teams move quickly but overlook details. Others gather extensive information before acting. Neither approach is inherently right or wrong, but awareness allows teams to make more intentional decisions about how they operate. The result is often better alignment, stronger execution, and increased organizational agility. In today’s business environment, where speed and collaboration are critical competitive advantages, team effectiveness cannot be viewed as a “soft skill.” It is a business capability. Organizations that intentionally invest in trust, alignment, and understanding create teams that can navigate complexity more effectively, adapt more quickly, and execute more consistently. Ultimately, that translates into better business outcomes.

title: Array Labs, Esper Satellite Imagery Announce Strategic Partnership to Co-Enrich Data
summary: Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery will co-enrich imagery to deliver a real-time, data-rich 3D map of Earth. Together, the two are committed to providing advanced, actionable, and affordable geospatial products to customers, driving growth in the commercial and government sectors alike.
body_text: Palo Alto, California, and Melbourne, Australia, March 13, 2024 – Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery today announced a strategic partnership to co-enrich each other's products, creating a powerful, one-of-a-kind dataset that combines high-resolution 3D with cutting-edge hyperspectral. The co-enrichment commitment allows both companies to provide even more value to their respective customers and markets. Under the terms of this agreement, users of Esper’s low-cost, extended-spectrum hyperspectral satellite imaging platform will be able to receive combined high-resolution 3D data. Similarly, Array’s customers will be able to combine and receive hyperspectral imagery with their 3D data purchases or subscriptions. This first-of-its-kind collaboration will empower customers to unlock previously unattainable insights, as they gain access to a comprehensive, multidimensional view of the Earth’s surface. By fusing Array Labs’ centimeter-level 3D data with Esper’s rich hyperspectral imagery, customers will not only be able to measure volumetric changes at scale, but also identify the precise materials driving those changes. The impact of this partnership will be felt across sectors: Energy and mining customers will be able to optimize operations; monitor infrastructure; and discover new exploration opportunities. Defense users will gain a powerful edge in identifying and analyzing objects of interest, with a new level of situational awareness. Environmental organizations and researchers will unlock a new tool to understand and protect our planet, using the multifaceted dataset to monitor ecosystems and track point-source emissions. BUILDING A REAL-TIME, DATA-RICH 3D MAP OF EARTH Array’s constellation, consisting of dozens of miniaturized, cost-effective radar satellites, is set to deliver a view of Earth in intricate 3D, with details down to the centimeter and unprecedented revisit rates. Meanwhile, Esper’s highly unique hyperspectral imagers capture up to 217 spectral bands at a remarkable 6-meter resolution, revisiting every corner of the globe every 10 days. Esper launched its first spacecraft – Over the Rainbow – last week aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-10 mission, with just under $1 million in pre-seed funding, the company told TechCrunch . Array Labs can confirm it will be launching its first three demonstrators – Kaladin, Rock, and Lopin – on Transporter-11 in just a few months. Around the same time, Esper will launch its second demonstrator with India’s ISRO. "Esper provides an immense spectral range not provided by others, very frequent revisit, and shares our passion for bringing high-value data from space in a highly affordable manner," said Array Labs CEO Andrew Peterson. "To our knowledge, this will be the first time 3D and hyperspectral imaging are combined and delivered from space for commercial use." "Esper and Array share the same ideology of launching with as low of a cost and as quickly as possible that challenges a lot of the status quo in the Earth Observation industry,” said Esper CEO Shoaib Iqbal. “This partnership further cements that, with a focus on the value both our companies can deliver together to solve customer problems." Together, Array Labs and Esper Satellite Imagery are committed to delivering the most advanced, actionable, and affordable geospatial products to customers, driving growth and innovation in the commercial and government sectors alike.

title: How does a swimming pool pump work?
summary: A swimming pool pump has a simple function: to circulate the water in the pool’s hydraulic network to pass it through the filter, thereby treating it.
body_text: A swimming pool pump has a simple function: to circulate the water in the pool’s hydraulic network to pass it through the filter, thereby treating it. Naturally, if it is the pump that sucks up and propels the water, it is extremely important that the hydraulic network must be designed correctly, in particular to avoid load losses and to pass as much water as possible through the filter. If this is the case, and you have chosen the pump that is suitable for your pool , it will then be able to provide you with the ideal flow rate for minimal energy expenditure. General swimming pool pump operation The core of a pump consists of a motor connected to a turbine: when turning, this sucks water from the pool skimmers. The water then enters through the front of the pump and firstly passes through a prefilter that captures residual debris and retains a useful reserve of water for priming the pump. While being sucked in, the water then enters the turbine, which pushes it towards the pump outlet. The water is now propelled : through the filter, then through any treatment devices and/or the heat pump, and finally to the nozzles that discharge the water into the pool. The cycle then starts again from the skimmers. The mechanical seal: an essential element for the lifespan of your pump A particularly important part of the pump is the mechanical seal , which ensures watertightness between the pump body (fixed) and the motor shaft (rotating). It is important that this mechanical seal - a rotating seal - is in water when the pump is started: otherwise, the seal may overheat and destroy itself in a few minutes. If your pump is below the level of your pool, don't worry, as it will always be loaded with water (naturally, if the water in the pool reaches the level of the skimmers and passes through the pipes, be careful about evaporation). However, if the pump is above your pool level, opt for a self-priming pump . This variant can suck up water even in the presence of air, thanks to its diffuser (yellow part in the diagram), which prevents the flow of pressure from returning to the front of the turbine, resulting in a considerable loss of efficiency. The rotating seal is a part that wears out logically with time and friction . Remember to replace it to preserve the motor and your pump's lifespan: replace it as soon as you see a leak. Don't panic, this is an inexpensive operation (the price of the seal) and accessible to anyone with a basic knowledge of DIY. More important than the pump: the hydraulic network design While the pump is naturally one of the main devices in the pool, it is still worth remembering that the most important thing is the design of its hydraulic network . To sufficiently filter the water every day, a certain flow rate is required. To ensure this flow, large pipes are especially useful, installed in order to avoid load losses between the skimmers and the pump (suction part). Remember that once the hydraulic network is buried, it is no longer accessible. Hence the importance of designing it well from the outset. Only when you feel assured that this network is well-designed, will you be able to choose a pump with a calm mind.

title: Expanding Mental Health Support
summary: See how CBIZ improved EAP outcomes with onsite, virtual, and telephonic counseling options that increased employee utilization.
body_text: Issue A government client was experiencing challenges with its Employee Assistance Program (EAP) as demand for accessible, cost-effective mental health resources continued to grow. Employees were increasingly seeking support for everyday life stressors, as well as specialized services tailored to the unique needs of first responders. To address these concerns, CBIZ partnered with its internal Wellbeing Practice to evaluate available solutions and identify an approach that would enhance employee support and better meet the evolving needs of the workforce. Solution CBIZ conducted a comprehensive evaluation of on-site counseling solutions to identify options that met the needs of the entire employee population, including the unique challenges faced by first responders. To ensure employees had access to appropriate and effective support, CBIZ assessed qualified providers and interviewed therapists with the specialized experience and credentials necessary to serve the client’s workforce. Outcome In the first year, the client implemented free on-site counseling services for all employees. Utilization increased by nearly 60% from program launch through year-end. Employee survey feedback was overwhelmingly positive, with many participants reporting personal benefits from the counseling services. To improve accessibility and accommodate scheduling constraints, the client expanded the program in year two to include telephonic and virtual counseling options. title: Look Up: Your AI Voyage Depends On It
summary: AI adoption is accelerating, but too many organizations remain focused on deployments and efficiencies rather than customer value. Learn why the most successful AI adopters build customer-focused strategies that drive trust, differentiation, and business outcomes.
body_text: Three years ago, the biggest question surrounding AI was whether organizations would adopt it. We now have the answer. Today, 77% of AI decision-makers report using agentic AI in production. AI is no longer an experiment. It has become part of how organizations work, innovate, and compete. Yet many leaders are confronting a new challenge: proving that AI investments deliver meaningful business value. Trust remains low, and many organizations still justify AI initiatives primarily through a productivity lens. Without a clear connection to outcomes, AI adoption can become expensive very quickly. The problem isn’t lack of activity, it’s that many organizations are looking down and inward. They are consumed by use cases, models, governance requirements, costs, and implementation challenges. They are focused on the next deployment, the next pilot, the next efficiency gain. Those efforts matter, but they can also distract from a more important question, one that should make you pause and look up and out to your customers — because they deserve it . What customer value are we trying to create? Organizations are moving quickly to embed AI into products, services, and operations. At the same time, customers and business buyers continue to scrutinize AI-generated outputs and expect clear evidence of value, reliability, and trustworthiness. What Sets High AI Adopters Apart? In a report we published earlier this year, Accelerate Your AI Voyage , we found that organizations generating the most momentum with AI understand the difference between adoption and value. They orient their AI strategies around customers rather than technology. Four traits consistently set them apart: Strong customer focus. They begin with customer needs and desired outcomes, then identify how AI can improve experiences, decisions, and results. CEO-driven AI vision and execution. CEOs actively champion AI initiatives and align investments to strategic business goals. Investment in AI-ready data and platforms. They build the data, governance, context, and technology foundations to scale AI effectively. High AIQ talent and skill development. They develop the skills, culture, and expertise required to work confidently with AI across the organization. Consider DBS Bank , which uses AI-powered recommendations to help customers make better financial decisions. Or Kraft Heinz , which applies genAI to create more relevant customer experiences while maintaining trust in its brand. These organizations aren’t using AI simply because they can. They’re using it to create value for their customers . As AI continues to evolve, organizations will continue to be bombarded with new models, agentic capabilities, and governance requirements, along with rising customer expectations. When organizations reconnect AI efforts to customer value, trust, and outcomes, they gain a reliable compass for navigating the complexity ahead. They stop measuring success by activity and start measuring success by impact. The companies that win with AI won’t necessarily be the ones deploying the most AI. They’ll be the ones that never lose sight of who the journey is for and constantly look up. Read Accelerate Your AI Voyage to learn how leading organizations are building customer-led, outcome-focused AI strategies that create value, build trust, and drive measurable business results. Join us at our AI Forums in Singapore and Sydney this August and at our Technology & Innovation Forums this fall as we explore how to close the gap from AI aspiration to AI advantage. (Cowritten with Anthony Andino, research associate) Share
